## Summary

E209 IT code entrant measurement complete. Produced 3 artifacts: tools/it_code_entrant_v2.py (measurement prototype, 306 lines), tools/it_entrant_advisor.py (entrant advisor with rankings, 352 lines), EXPERIMENTS/E209-it-code-entrant/RESULT.md (experiment record, 102 lines). Key achievement: applied E208's NIH SBIR entrant-measurement design to federal IT USAspending PSC codes, revealing a bimodal entry pattern — unlike NIH SBIR's unimodal common-entry (median 0.527 frag-indep), federal IT shows 2 codes with significant entry (DA01: 0.2677, 7A21: 0.2912), 1 surviving the 0.30 kill gate (DA10: 0.3113), and 2 with 0 newcomers (7030, D304 — all recipients pre-existing). This closes the 'fragmented ⇒ entry' inference transfer claim from E208. The entrant-attractiveness score (segment_frac × obligation_billions) ranks: DA01 > DA10 > 7A21 > 7030 > D304. Remaining unknown: whether bimodal pattern holds across more PSC codes. Single most useful next action: validate pattern robustness with additional PSC codes, or pursue fresh observation in new domain per D083.
